question: Find some papers that discuss the methods to suppress multiple light scattering effect on light scattering imaging

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies multi-focus averaging as a method for suppressing multiple scattering in optical coherence tomography by combining images captured at different focal depths.
examples: Multi-focus averaging integrates images at various focal depths to reduce multiple scattering artifacts in OCT
Combining OCT images taken at multiple focal depths improves clarity and contrast in highly scattering biological tissues

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies the digital camera-based detection approach used in dynamic light scattering to suppress multiple scattering by selectively capturing ballistic photons.
examples: A digital camera detection scheme in dynamic light scattering selectively captures ballistic photons in turbid media
Digital camera-based detection suppresses multiple scattering, enhancing accuracy of dynamic measurements in turbid media

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies cross-correlation as a technique that differentiates and suppresses multiply scattered photons using the statistical properties of scattered light.
examples: Cross-correlation methods distinguish single from multiple scattering events by analyzing statistical properties of scattered light
Cross-correlation suppresses multiply scattered photons and improves signal-to-noise ratio in optical measurements

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer correctly attributes each method to its modality: multi-focus averaging to OCT and the camera scheme to dynamic light scattering, presenting at least two distinct papers/methods (survey-style synthesis).
examples: Multi-focus averaging is used in optical coherence tomography
The digital camera scheme applies to dynamic light scattering in turbid media
Three techniques are discussed: multi-focus averaging, digital camera detection, and cross-correlation

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains at least one suppression mechanism in terms of photon selection or differentiation, e.g., capturing ballistic photons or statistically separating single from multiple scattering events.
examples: Ballistic photons are selectively captured to reject multiply scattered light
The statistical properties of scattered light are used to separate single and multiple scattering events

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: For each method mentioned, the answer states the resulting benefit such as improved image clarity, contrast, resolution, signal-to-noise ratio, or measurement accuracy and reliability.
examples: Multi-focus averaging leads to improved image clarity and contrast in OCT
Cross-correlation improves the signal-to-noise ratio in optical measurements
Digital camera detection enhances the accuracy and reliability of dynamic measurements

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer specifies the scattering context in which methods apply, such as highly scattering biological tissues or turbid media.
examples: Multi-focus averaging is especially effective in highly scattering biological tissues
The digital camera scheme works in turbid media

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer frames the methods collectively as a body of techniques developed to mitigate the adverse effects of multiple light scattering, enabling clearer, more reliable imaging in scattering media.
examples: Several techniques have been developed to mitigate the adverse effects of multiple scattering
Collectively, these methods enable clearer imaging in scattering media
